portAccess: Port of Houston — one of the busiest ports in the U.S. with direct rail connections via UP and BNSF.
description: Houston is one of America's largest rail freight hubs, anchored by Union Pacific and BNSF operations that connect the petrochemical corridor along the Gulf Coast to markets nationwide. The city's rail network handles massive volumes of petroleum products, chemicals, and plastics from the surrounding refinery complex, along with grain exports moving through the Port of Houston.

Chicago is the undisputed rail capital of North America, where all six Class I railroads converge. Roughly 25% of all U.S. rail traffic passes through the Chicago terminal district. The city's classification yards, transload facilities, and interchange points make it the critical junction for east-west and north-south freight flows across the continent.

Atlanta is the Southeast's primary rail hub, served by both Norfolk Southern and CSX. Norfolk Southern's Inman Yard is one of the largest classification yards in the eastern U.S. The city serves as a critical interchange point for freight moving between the Port of Savannah and inland markets throughout the Southeast and Midwest.

Dallas-Fort Worth is a major rail crossroads in the southern U.S., with BNSF, Union Pacific, and Canadian Pacific Kansas City all maintaining significant operations. The BNSF Alliance facility north of Fort Worth is one of the nation's largest inland freight hubs, and the metro area serves as a key distribution point for goods moving across the Sun Belt.

Kansas City sits at the crossroads of four Class I railroads, making it one of the most important rail junctions in the central U.S. The city is a major gateway for grain moving from the Great Plains to export markets and for merchandise freight flowing between the coasts. BNSF's Argentine Yard is one of the largest classification yards in the nation.

portAccess: Port of Memphis on the Mississippi River with rail-barge transfer capabilities.
description: Memphis is a top-tier rail hub where five Class I railroads converge along the Mississippi River. The city's strategic position connects the western and eastern rail networks, and its terminals handle enormous freight volumes in both directions. Rail-barge interchange along the Mississippi adds another dimension to Memphis's logistics capabilities.

portAccess: Port of Los Angeles and Port of Long Beach — the nation's busiest container port complex with dedicated on-dock rail facilities.
description: Los Angeles is the western gateway for international trade, with the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach generating massive rail volumes. BNSF and Union Pacific operate major yards that funnel freight from Asia-Pacific trade routes onto transcontinental rail corridors serving the entire U.S. market.

portAccess: Port of St. Louis on the Mississippi River — major rail-barge interchange point.
description: St. Louis is a critical Mississippi River crossing point where eastern and western railroads interchange freight. The city's bridge connections across the river make it a natural bottleneck and interchange hub. Coal, grain, and chemicals move heavily through St. Louis, and the rail-barge transfer facilities along the river support bulk commodity logistics.

portAccess: Port of New Orleans and Port of South Louisiana — among the world's largest by tonnage, with extensive rail-to-vessel transfer facilities.
description: New Orleans sits at the mouth of the Mississippi River where five Class I railroads converge with one of the world's busiest port complexes. The region is a global export gateway for grain, coal, and petroleum products. Rail lines along the river corridor connect the Gulf Coast refineries and chemical plants to markets throughout North America.

portAccess: JAXPORT — growing container port with on-dock rail capabilities.
description: Jacksonville is CSX's hometown and the rail gateway to Florida. The city's terminals handle merchandise freight destined for the Florida peninsula, along with phosphate moving from central Florida mines. JAXPORT's expanding container operations are adding international trade volumes to the city's rail network.

portAccess: Port of Virginia (Norfolk International Terminals, Virginia International Gateway) — major East Coast deep-water port with double-stack rail access.
description: Norfolk is Norfolk Southern's namesake city and a critical coal export terminal. Lamberts Point is the largest coal transloading facility in the Northern Hemisphere, loading coal onto vessels for international export. The Port of Virginia's marine terminals also feature excellent rail connectivity for import and export traffic.

Omaha is the headquarters of Union Pacific Railroad and a major gateway for agricultural commodities moving from the Great Plains. The nearby Bailey Yard in North Platte is the world's largest classification yard. Omaha's rail infrastructure supports heavy grain, ethanol, and fertilizer traffic serving the agricultural heartland.

Fort Worth is BNSF's headquarters city and home to the Alliance logistics hub, one of the largest inland ports in the country. The Tower 55 junction, where BNSF and UP lines cross, is one of the most critical rail bottlenecks in North America. Major investments are underway to improve rail fluidity through this corridor.

San Antonio sits on major Union Pacific and BNSF corridors connecting the Texas-Mexico border region with the interior U.S. The city handles significant building materials and petroleum products traffic, and its proximity to the Eagle Ford Shale region drives energy-related rail shipments.

Nashville is a growing rail hub in the mid-South served by CSX and Norfolk Southern. CSX's Radnor Yard is a key classification facility for freight moving through the Tennessee Valley. The city's booming economy is driving increased freight volumes and distribution center development along rail corridors.

Charlotte is a key rail hub in the Piedmont region served by Norfolk Southern and CSX. The city anchors a major freight corridor connecting the Port of Charleston and inland Southeast markets. Charlotte's growing population and distribution sector are driving increased rail freight demand.

Columbus is a major freight hub in the Midwest, anchored by Norfolk Southern's Rickenbacker terminal — one of the busiest inland rail facilities in the eastern U.S. The city's central Ohio location makes it a natural distribution point for consumer goods serving the eastern half of the country.

Indianapolis is a crossroads for CSX and Norfolk Southern freight in the heart of the Midwest. The city's central location makes it a natural hub for automotive parts, grain, and merchandise freight. CSX's Avon Yard handles classification of railcars moving between eastern and midwestern markets.

Minneapolis-St. Paul is a major northern rail hub where four Class I railroads converge. The Twin Cities are a critical gateway for grain from the upper Midwest, iron ore from the Mesabi Range, and potash imports from Canada. BNSF's Northtown Yard is a major classification facility.

Detroit is a critical cross-border rail gateway connecting the U.S. and Canadian rail networks via the Detroit-Windsor tunnel and Ambassador Bridge corridor. The city's automotive industry drives massive rail volumes of auto parts, finished vehicles, and steel. Four Class I railroads serve the Detroit metro area.

portAccess: Port of Cleveland on Lake Erie — handles iron ore and bulk materials via Great Lakes shipping.
description: Cleveland is a legacy steel and heavy industry rail hub on the southern shore of Lake Erie. CSX and Norfolk Southern handle significant volumes of steel, iron ore, and coal through the metro area. The Port of Cleveland provides lake vessel-to-rail interchange for bulk commodities arriving via the Great Lakes.

Cincinnati is a key Ohio River rail crossing served by CSX and Norfolk Southern. CSX's Queensgate Yard is a major classification facility in the eastern network. The city's position at the intersection of north-south and east-west rail corridors makes it an important freight interchange point.

Pittsburgh sits at the confluence of three rivers and has been a rail freight hub since the earliest days of American railroading. CSX's Conway Yard is one of the largest classification yards in the eastern U.S. The region's legacy in coal and steel continues to drive significant rail volumes, alongside growing merchandise traffic.

portAccess: Port of Baltimore — major auto import port and coal export facility with direct rail service.
description: Baltimore is a key East Coast port city served by CSX and Norfolk Southern. The Port of Baltimore is the nation's top auto import port and a significant coal export terminal. CSX's Howard Street Tunnel is being expanded to accommodate double-stack trains, which will dramatically increase capacity through the corridor.

portAccess: PhilaPort — growing marine port with rail connections for inbound and outbound freight.
description: Philadelphia is a major Northeast rail hub served by CSX and Norfolk Southern. The city's refineries along the Delaware River generate petroleum and chemical rail traffic, while PhilaPort handles growing container volumes. The Northeast Corridor's proximity creates both passenger and freight rail congestion challenges that shape operations.

portAccess: Port of Savannah (Garden City Terminal) — the fastest-growing container port in the U.S. with massive on-terminal rail infrastructure.
description: Savannah is home to one of America's fastest-growing container ports, and rail plays a critical role in moving containers inland. Norfolk Southern and CSX both serve the port, with NS operating a major terminal that connects Savannah to Atlanta, the Midwest, and beyond. The port's expansion is driving record rail volumes.

portAccess: Port of Charleston — deep-water container port with dedicated rail-served inland port at Dillon, SC.
description: Charleston is a growing Southeast port city where CSX and Norfolk Southern connect international container trade to inland markets. The South Carolina Ports Authority has invested heavily in rail infrastructure, including the Inland Port at Dillon, which extends the port's reach into the Carolinas and Virginia via Norfolk Southern rail service.

portAccess: Port of Mobile — deep-water port on Mobile Bay handling coal, steel, and containerized freight.
description: Mobile is a Gulf Coast port city served by three Class I railroads: CSX, Norfolk Southern, and Canadian National. The Port of Mobile handles coal exports, steel imports, and growing container volumes. CN's rail corridor from Mobile to Chicago provides a direct north-south route for Gulf Coast freight.

portAccess: Port of Greater Baton Rouge on the Mississippi River — major petrochemical and grain handling facility.
description: Baton Rouge anchors a massive petrochemical corridor along the Mississippi River between New Orleans and the capital. Union Pacific and Canadian National serve the region's refineries and chemical plants, moving petroleum products, plastics, and chemicals by rail. The port handles significant grain and fertilizer volumes as well.

portAccess: Port of Beaumont and Port Arthur — major petroleum and military cargo handling ports with rail service.
description: Beaumont sits in the heart of the Texas Golden Triangle petrochemical region, served by Union Pacific, BNSF, and Canadian Pacific Kansas City. The Port of Beaumont is one of the nation's top military cargo ports and handles significant petroleum and chemical rail traffic from the surrounding refinery complex.

El Paso is one of the busiest U.S.-Mexico rail border crossings, with BNSF and Union Pacific operating international gateways that connect to Mexican rail networks. Cross-border trade drives massive merchandise and automotive volumes. The city is a critical link in the supply chain connecting Mexican manufacturing with U.S. markets.

Denver is the primary rail hub for the Rocky Mountain region, served by BNSF and Union Pacific. The city sits at the base of the Front Range where coal from the Powder River Basin and grain from the High Plains funnel through en route to western and eastern markets. Denver's growing population is also driving increased freight demand.

Salt Lake City is the intermountain West's rail hub, where Union Pacific and BNSF corridors converge between the Sierra Nevada and Rocky Mountains. The region's mining industry drives coal, copper, and industrial mineral rail volumes, while the city's growing economy supports increasing merchandise traffic.

portAccess: Port of Portland — grain export terminal and container facility on the Columbia River with rail access.
description: Portland is the Pacific Northwest's primary rail hub, served by BNSF and Union Pacific. The Port of Portland's grain elevators export wheat and other grains from the Columbia Basin and Great Plains. The city also handles lumber and forest products rail traffic from the surrounding timber region.

portAccess: Port of Seattle and Port of Tacoma (Northwest Seaport Alliance) — major Asia-Pacific trade gateway with on-dock rail.
description: Seattle-Tacoma is the Pacific Northwest's international trade gateway, with BNSF and Union Pacific connecting the ports to transcontinental rail corridors. The Northwest Seaport Alliance handles massive container volumes from Asia-Pacific trade routes, and BNSF's northern transcontinental corridor provides competitive transit times to the Midwest.

portAccess: Port of Shreveport-Bossier on the Red River with rail-barge transfer capabilities.
description: Shreveport is a north Louisiana rail junction served by Union Pacific and Canadian Pacific Kansas City. The city sits at the crossroads of east-west and north-south rail corridors, handling petroleum products, chemicals, and forest products. The Haynesville Shale natural gas region drives energy-related rail traffic through the area.

Birmingham has deep roots as a rail and steel city, with three Class I railroads serving the metro area. Norfolk Southern's Boyles Yard is a major classification facility for coal and steel moving through the Southeast. The region's legacy iron and steel industries continue to drive significant rail volumes alongside growing merchandise traffic.

portAccess: Port of Little Rock on the Arkansas River with rail-barge interchange.
description: Little Rock is central Arkansas's rail hub, served by Union Pacific and BNSF. The city sits on the Arkansas River where rail and barge freight interchange. Agricultural products, lumber, and steel move through Little Rock's rail terminals, connecting the mid-South region to national rail networks.

Jackson is Mississippi's primary rail junction where Canadian National, Norfolk Southern, and CSX converge. CN's north-south corridor connects the Gulf Coast to Memphis, Chicago, and Canada, making Jackson a strategic interchange point. The city handles forest products, chemicals, and petroleum traffic serving the central Mississippi region.

Hattiesburg is a south Mississippi rail junction where Canadian National and Norfolk Southern lines intersect. The city serves the region's timber and paper industries, with forest products representing a major share of rail volume. CN's mainline through Hattiesburg connects the Gulf Coast ports to Jackson and points north.

Meridian is a historic rail junction in east Mississippi where Norfolk Southern and Canadian National share the Meridian Speedway — a high-capacity corridor connecting Meridian to Shreveport. The Speedway allows NS trains to bypass congested routes, making Meridian a strategic point for merchandise freight moving between the Southeast and Texas.

Laurel is a small Mississippi city on the Norfolk Southern mainline with deep roots in the timber industry. Rail freight through Laurel consists primarily of forest products, paper, and chemicals. The city's NS connection provides access to the broader eastern rail network via Meridian and beyond.

portAccess: Port of Gulfport — Mississippi's only deep-water seaport with rail connections for bulk and breakbulk cargo.
description: Gulfport is a Mississippi Gulf Coast port city served by CSX. The Port of Gulfport is the state's only deep-water seaport and handles forest products, frozen poultry, and breakbulk cargo with direct rail access. CSX's Gulf Coast mainline connects Gulfport to New Orleans and Jacksonville.

portAccess: Port of Tuscaloosa on the Black Warrior-Tombigbee Waterway with rail-barge transfer.
description: Tuscaloosa is a western Alabama rail hub served by three Class I railroads. The Mercedes-Benz U.S. International assembly plant generates significant automotive rail traffic, including inbound parts and outbound finished vehicles. The region's coal and timber industries add to the rail freight mix.

Montgomery is a central Alabama rail junction served by CSX and Norfolk Southern. The Hyundai Motor Manufacturing Alabama plant near Montgomery generates significant automotive rail traffic. The city's position on CSX's main north-south corridor connects it to the Port of Mobile and Birmingham.

Knoxville is an east Tennessee rail hub served by Norfolk Southern and CSX. The city sits at the junction of rail corridors passing through the Appalachian coal fields, handling significant coal traffic from eastern Kentucky and Virginia mines. NS's mainline through Knoxville connects the Southeast to the Ohio Valley.

Chattanooga is a critical rail junction in southeast Tennessee where Norfolk Southern operates one of its key terminals. The city sits at the intersection of NS corridors connecting Atlanta, Knoxville, and Nashville, making it a strategic interchange point for merchandise freight. The Volkswagen assembly plant adds automotive rail volumes.

portAccess: Port of Louisville on the Ohio River with rail-barge interchange for bulk commodities.
description: Louisville is a major Ohio River rail hub served by CSX and Norfolk Southern. The city's Ford assembly plants and UPS Worldport distribution hub drive significant automotive and consumer goods rail traffic. Louisville also handles bourbon and spirits shipments from the surrounding Kentucky distillery region, along with coal from Appalachian mines.

Billings is the largest city in Montana and a key point on BNSF's northern transcontinental corridor. The nearby Laurel Yard is BNSF's main classification facility in the region. Coal from the Powder River Basin, petroleum products from Montana and North Dakota refineries, and grain from the northern Great Plains dominate rail traffic through Billings.

Amarillo sits on BNSF's Southern Transcon — one of the busiest freight rail corridors in the world connecting Los Angeles to Chicago. The Texas Panhandle city handles grain, cattle feed, and petroleum products from the surrounding agricultural and energy regions. BNSF's high-priority freight trains pass through Amarillo daily on the Transcon route.
